issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/main/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L355


# Vulnerability details


`BondingManager.sol` have 2 mathUtils libraries, `MathUtils` use 1e6 as precision while `PreciseMathUtils` use 1e27 as precision.
Some variable use `MathUtils` while other use `PreciseMathUtils` which might cause confusion.
It happen with `treasuryRewardCutRate` variable which require `PreciseMathUtils` [(comment)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/main/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L97-L98) but mistakenly use `MathUtils` instead on this [specific line](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/main/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L355)

## Impact

Function `updateTranscoderWithFees()` not workinga as intended and always revert when calling twice for current round.

## Proof of Concept

```js
    // Deduct what would have been the treasury rewards
    uint256 treasuryRewards = MathUtils.percOf(rewards, treasuryRewardCutRate);//@audit M treasury rate is 1e27. Here it is 1e6
    rewards = rewards.sub(treasuryRewards);//@note reward now send some percentage to treasury
```

`treasuryRewardCutRate` decimal value is 1e27 which suppose to use with `PreciseMathUtils.percOf` for all operation.

[Like implemented in `rewardWithHint()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/b4a655e6888242ec98ce0e9d6213ef683c854861/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L883) from same contract.

`treasuryRewardCutRate` is 0.1e27 in config

So this second line `rewards = rewards - (rewards * treasuryRewardCutRate /1e6)` always underflow and revert.

## Tools Used
manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Change `MathUtils` to `PreciseMathUtils`

```js
    // Deduct what would have been the treasury rewards
    uint256 treasuryRewards = PreciseMathUtils.percOf(rewards, treasuryRewardCutRate);
    rewards = rewards.sub(treasuryRewards);
```



## Assessed type

Decimal

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

## Proof of Concept
In the _handleVoteOverrides function, the deductions are added to the transcoder's voter state without any validation: https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/treasury/GovernorCountingOverridable.sol#L192-L193
A malicious delegator could call _countVote multiple times, each time increasing the deductions for the transcoder. This would reduce the effective vote weight of the transcoder when they actually vote.

For example, if a transcoder has 100 tokens staked, a malicious delegator could call _countVote pretending to be a delegator and add 1000 to deductions. Now when the transcoder votes, their effective weight will only be 100 - 1000 = -900 tokens. This could incorrectly make a proposal fail or succeed.

## Tools Used
Manual 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
_handleVoteOverrides should validate that the _weight being deducted from the transcoder is less than or equal to the transcoder's actual voting weight. 
Note* The same validation should also be added when deducting delegator weights in the main _countVote function.

Other

issues.title: The quorum calculation in the _quorumReached() function is inconsistent and could allow abstain votes to prevent a proposal from reaching quorum even if most participating voters are in favor
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/treasury/GovernorCountingOverridable.sol#L110-L112


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This allows abstain voters to effectively veto a proposal, even if most participating voters approve it.

## Proof of Concept
The quorum numerator and denominator are inconsistent. The quorum uses totalVotes for the denominator which includes abstains. But the numerator is just forVotes + againstVotes. This means a large number of abstain votes could prevent a quorum even if most participating voters are for.T

The quorum denominator is totalVotes, which includes abstain votes. But the quorum numerator only counts againstVotes and forVotes.

This means if there are a large number of abstain votes, the quorum condition could fail even if most participating voters voted in favor.

For example:

Total votes: 100
For votes: 60
Against votes: 10
Abstain votes: 30
Even though 60% of participating voters voted in favor, the quorum check would be:

60 + 10 >= quorum(100)

So with a quorum requirement of 51% for example, this proposal would fail to reach quorum.

This allows abstain voters to effectively veto a proposal, even if most participating voters approve it.

## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
the quorum numerator should also include abstain votes

Other

issues.title: bonding on behalf of a new delegator sets the start round to the current round + 1, but the assumed future round may never actually start if rounds get stuck
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L569
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L585


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
• If rounds get stuck and currentRound + 1 never happens, the new delegator will never be able to claim earnings. Their startRound will be set to a future round that doesn't exist.
• This prevents them from claiming earnings accrued from their staked tokens.

## Proof of Concept
When bonding on behalf of a new delegator, it sets the start round to the current round + 1. But this assumes the current round will actually end and the next one will start. If rounds get stuck or the protocol runs into issues, this assumed future round may never happen

del.startRound is set to currentRound + 1. This assumes that currentRound will end and a new round (currentRound + 1) will start.

• If rounds get stuck and currentRound + 1 never happens, the new delegator will never be able to claim earnings. Their startRound will be set to a future round that doesn't exist.
• This prevents them from claiming earnings accrued from their staked tokens.

## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
• Could set the startRound to currentRound instead of currentRound + 1. This guarantees the delegator can start claiming earnings in the current round rather than relying on a future round.
• Or add a check if currentRound + 1 exists before setting startRound. If it doesn't exist yet, set startRound to currentRound.



## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: .The _newPosPrev/_newPosNext hints do not fully prevent invalid ordering when decreasing a delegate's stake.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1363
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1367


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The contract could incorrectly deactivate or reward transcoders based on the invalid pool order. 

## Proof of Concept
When decreasing a delegate's stake with decreaseTotalStake(), the contract calls transcoderPool.updateKey() to update the delegate's position in the pool. However, passing the _newPosPrev/_newPosNext hints does not guarantee correct ordering after the update.
Here is how an invalid order could occur:
1. Transcoder A has 1000 LPT stake, Transcoder B has 500 LPT stake
2. The pool order is: [A, B]
3. B's stake decreases to 400 LPT
4. We pass A as the _newPosPrev hint when updating B's stake
5. This positions B before A in the pool even though A has higher stake
6. Resulting invalid order: [B, A]


## Tools Used
Manual 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Proper mitigations include doing a full sort after updates or maintaining a separate sorted list for validation.

Other

issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1442-L1443

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This will result in the total active stake being incorrectly calculated in future rounds. Some transcoders may get more or less rewards than they should.

## Proof of Concept
The key functions involved are:
- slashTranscoder - Called to slash a transcoder. Reduces the transcoder's stake and removes it from the pool if active.
- decreaseTotalStake - Decreases the total stake for a transcoder. Called by slashTranscoder.
- resignTranscoder - Removes a transcoder from the pool and deactivates it.

The issue is that slashTranscoder calls decreaseTotalStake unconditionally, even if the transcoder was already deactivated. 

In Summary 

The key points:
- slashTranscoder calls resignTranscoder to deactivate the transcoder and remove from pool
- But it still calls decreaseTotalStake after, even if already deactivated
-  decreaseTotalStake reduces the nextRoundTotalActiveStake

So if the transcoder was already deactivated, decreaseTotalStake incorrectly reduces the total stake again.


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
This can be fixed by checking if the transcoder is already deactivated before calling decreaseTotalStake()

A transcoder can potentially receive rewards/fees when it should not be active anymore

This means the transcoder could still be improperly considered active and receive rewards/fees for part of the round after it called resignTranscoder().

Manual

resignTranscoder() should set deactivationRound to the current round instead of next round:

issues.title: Underflow in updateTranscoderWithFees can cause corrupted data and loss of winning tickets.
using increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() instead of increaseTotalStake() can lead to inconsistent transcoder state
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1488
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1459


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This allows a transcoder to increase their voting power without actually increasing their stake.

## Proof of Concept
The relevant code that uses increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() and skips transcoder state checkpointing is in the updateTranscoderWithRewards() function: https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1488

Using increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() instead of increaseTotalStake() can lead to inconsistent transcoder state.
The key difference is that increaseTotalStake() has an autoCheckpoint modifier which calls _checkpointBondingState(), while increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() does not.
_checkpointBondingState() updates the historical record of the transcoder's stake and reward state via the BondingVotes contract. This historical record is used for calculating voting power in the governance system.
By skipping the checkpoint, increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() causes the transcoder's voting power to become inconsistent with its actual stake.
For example:
1. Transcoder A has 100 LPT bonded, last reward round 10
2. Call increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed(A, 50 LPT)
3. A now has 150 LPT bonded, but BondingVotes still records A as having 100 LPT at round 10
4. A's voting power will be calculated incorrectly based on the outdated BondingVotes records


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps 
increaseTotalStakeUncheckpointed() should only be used in cases where the caller guarantees it will checkpoint the state later, like in processRebond(). For general stake increases, increaseTotalStake() should be used.


## Assessed type

Other

issues.title: The bond manager contract  does not properly zero out the transcoder's cumulative rewards/fees between rounds.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1534-L1538


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
transcoder's cumulative rewards and fees can continue accumulating from previous rounds, instead of resetting each round. This means a transcoder could claim portion of rewards/fees that it should not be entitled to.

## Proof of Concept
This only resets the cumulative rewards and fees to 0 if the delegator is claiming for themselves (self-delegated). For normal delegators, it does not reset these values.
Over multiple rounds, this could allow the transcoder's cumulative rewards and fees to keep growing, even if delegators are claiming and withdrawing the rewards.
For example:
• Round 1: 
o  Transcoder earns 100 rewards
o  Delegator claims and withdraws 50 rewards
• Transcoder cumulativeRewards = 100
• Round 2: 
o  Transcoder earns 50 more rewards
o  Delegator claims and withdraws 100 rewards
•  Transcoder cumulativeRewards = 150
Even though the delegator withdrew all the rewards they earned, the transcoder's cumulativeRewards keeps growing.
This could incorrectly increase the transcoder's stake and position in the pool over time. It also means the cumulative factors used to calculate delegator earnings could be inflated.

In summary, this resets the cumulative rewards and fees to 0 when a delegator claims earnings, but only if the delegator is claiming for itself (is the transcoder). It does not reset these values when another delegator claims.


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The cumulative values should be reset for the transcoder at the end of every round, regardless of who is claiming earnings


## Assessed type

Other

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L384

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
This could lead to incorrect fee calculations for delegators when claiming fees or pending fees.
First time earnings are calculated in the new round, they will use the old cumulative fee factor rather than starting from 0 as intended. This effectively pays out some fees twice to delegators.

## Proof of Concept
True, this is a potential issue in the code.
The key parts are:
1. lastFeeRound is only updated when fees are added in updateTranscoderWithFees():https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L384

So when updateTranscoderWithFees() is first called in a new round, lastFeeRound will still be the previous round. This means latestCumulativeFactorsPool() will return the fee factor for the previous round, not the current round.

Manual

 lastFeeRound couuld be reset to 0 in reward() along with the other earnings tracking fields like cumulativeFees. This would ensure it starts fresh

issues.title: Slashing transcoders on violation should not effect the delegators who staked into such transcoders, delegators should  continue to earn rewards
Incorrect usage of an uninitialized earnings pool if lastRewardRound >= currentRound.
issues.body:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L321
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L327
https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-08-livepeer/blob/a3d801fa4690119b6f96aeb5508e58d752bda5bc/contracts/bonding/BondingManager.sol#L1519-L1520


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If lastRewardRound >= currentRound, the earningsPool for currentRound may not be initialized if reward() has not yet been called for currentRound. So using it to update cumulative rewards or fees could be incorrect.
This can lead to incorrect reward calculations for delegators. For example, if the cumulativeRewardFactor is 0 when it should be non-zero, delegators will get 0 rewards.

## Proof of Concept
The vulnerability occurs in pendingStakeAndFees() when _endRound = currentRound and lastRewardRound >= currentRound.

In this case, endEarningsPool will not be initialized because lastRewardRound >= currentRound. But then endEarningsPool is still used to calculate cumulative factors, even though it was never initialized. This could lead to using uninitialized (zero) cumulative factor values and incorrect reward calculations.

A proof of concept:
- Call updateTranscoderWithFees() in round 10
- This sets lastRewardRound = 10
- Call pendingStakeAndFees() in round 10, with _endRound = 10
- endEarningsPool = t.earningsPoolPerRound[10] is uninitialized because lastRewardRound (10) >= currentRound (10)
- pendingStakeAndFees still uses the uninitialized endEarningsPool for calculations


## Tools Used
Manual
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
A check in pendingStakeAndFees() to initialize endEarningsPool if lastRewardRound >= _endRound


## Assessed type

Other
